sn15.20:2.3: A _pācīnavaṁsa_ was a hall or shed built for the ritual, with bamboo (_vaṁsa_) beams running easterly (_pācīna_; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 3.1.1.6 and Eggeling’s note). Perhaps the mountain was noted as the site for the introduction of this ritual institution. In the Buddha’s day, there was an “Park of the East-Raftered Hall” in Cetī ([mn128:8.1](), [an8.30:1.2]()).
sn15.20:2.4: _Tivara_ may be connected to Vedic _trivarūtha_, the “triple defence” granted devotees by the gods. By Vedic times this acquired a religious sense, but probably originated in fortifications; see the three defenses guarding Pokkharasāti: armed guards, walls, and moat ([dn3:2.10.11]()).
sn15.20:5.5: Note the arthasastra counts 15 muhurtas per day, and 15 per night. So “hour” is not too bad.
